summaryBox.title: Topology Takeaway
summaryBox.takeaway: An open interval with identical endpoints (a, a) = ∅, whereas [a, a] = {a} is a singleton set.

INTERVAL TYPES ON THE REAL LINE
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┴──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
OPEN INTERVAL          CLOSED INTERVAL               HALF-OPEN INTERVAL  UNBOUNDED INTERVAL
(a, b)                 [a, b]                        (a, b] or [a, b)    (a, ∞) or (-∞, b]
{x | a < x < b}        {x | a ≤ x ≤ b}               {x | a < x ≤ b}     {x | x > a}
conceptBreakdown.content:
Subsets of the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ are frequently represented using **Interval Notation**. Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$:

### Master Interval Classification Table

| Interval Notation | Set-Builder Definition | Boundary Included? | Boundedness |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Open:** $(a, b)$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid a < x < b\}$ | Neither $a$ nor $b$ | Bounded |
| **Closed:** $[a, b]$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid a \le x \le b\}$ | Both $a$ and $b$ | Bounded |
| **Left-Closed, Right-Open:** $[a, b)$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid a \le x < b\}$ | $a$ included, $b$ excluded | Bounded |
| **Left-Open, Right-Closed:** $(a, b]$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid a < x \le b\}$ | $a$ excluded, $b$ included | Bounded |
| **Unbounded Above:** $[a, \infty)$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \ge a\}$ | $a$ included | Unbounded |
| **Unbounded Below:** $(-\infty, b)$ | $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x < b\}$ | $b$ excluded | Unbounded |
| **Entire Real Line:** $(-\infty, \infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ | None | Unbounded |
